newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY OTP SEC YEAR-END BUX TARGET 8,000-8,200PTS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY OTP SEC YEAR-END BUX TARGET 8,000-8,200PTS.

text.p: Hungary's OTP Securities, the investment arm of the OTP financial group, said on Thursday that its year-end target for the BUX index was 8,000 to 8,200 points.
On Wednesday the BUX index finished at a sixth successive record high gf 7,296.64 points, while on Thursday it opened lower.
In a country report OTP Securities said corporate earnings will be the driving force this year.

"In 1997, gains will be based on company performance rather than on the relative undervaluation of the stock exchange overall, which has been the case in prior years," said the report, prepared by equit9 analyst Gabor Korondan and macroeconomics anal9st Peter Bozso.
"The market can also expect to benefit from the redirection of capital to Hungary from other Visegrad countries," the report added.
Hungary, Poland, the Czech Republic and Slovakia make up the group of the Visegrad countries.
Market participants have often said recently that fresh capital flew into the Budapest Stock Exchange due to economic concerns in the Czech Republic and in Poland.
OTP Securities suggested investors should base investments on pgtentials of individual companies.
"Investment on the exchange should be based on a particular company's potential for growth in export sales and by its possibilities for regional expansion."
